beliefs: f(x) inserts the letter 'i' into the input string [E1, E2]
For two-character strings, 'i' is inserted after the first character: 'ab'->'aib', 'AB'->'AiB' [E1]
For longer strings, 'i' is inserted at index len//2 (floor), e.g. 'abcdef'->'abcidef', '123456'->'123i456' [E2]
Leading spaces appear to be stripped before insertion: '  x'->'i x', ' x'->'ix', '   x'->'i x', '    x'->'i  x', '  ab'->'iab', ' ab'->'iab' [E3]
After stripping, insertion is at index len//2 of the stripped string [E3]
For ' x ' (stripped to 'x', len 1) output is 'ix' = 'i'+'x', consistent with single-char rule [E3]
For 'a  b' (len 4, no leading/trailing spaces) output 'a i b' = insert at index 2 = len//2 [E3]
notes: Discovered that leading and trailing spaces are stripped before the insert-at-len//2 rule is applied; this explains all E3 outputs including '  x'->'i x' and '   '->'i'.
